lesson.title: 911 – Procedure 104: Event Creation Codes (10-01 to 10-09)
objectives: Explain the purpose and five main areas covered by Procedure 104 radio codes.
Correctly identify and use event-creation codes 10-01 through 10-07.
Recognize when 10-08 and 10-09 are NOT used.
Apply the special instructions tied to event-creation codes (e.g., when NOT to use 10-04).

questions.stem: According to Procedure 104, radio code signals are used by dispatchers to cover which FIVE primary areas?

choices.text: Event creation, vehicle checks, out of service, interim status, and final dispositions.
Crimes in progress, patrol supervision, training, payroll, and vacations.
Only crimes in progress and priority incidents.
Only final dispositions and out-of-service statuses.

questions.solution: Procedure 104 states that radio codes are used for event creation, vehicle checks, out of service, interim status, and final dispositions.

questions.stem: A unit needs to be told to call their own command, not the dispatcher. Which code should be transmitted?
questions.solution: 10-01 is used to tell a unit to CALL YOUR COMMAND, and the message should not come over the dispatcher’s air from the command.

questions.stem: Code 10-04 ACKNOWLEDGMENT may be used when a transmission was not heard or understood.
Codes 10-08 and 10-09 are marked as NOT USED in Procedure 104.
Code 10-03 CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE requires the dispatcher to transmit the __________ at the same time if it is unknown to the unit.
Code 10-07 VERIFY ADDRESS is only used when a dispatcher wants to know the unit’s current __________.
Match each event-creation code with its correct description.
answer: CALL YOUR COMMAND (message should not come over dispatcher’s air from the command).
REPORT TO YOUR COMMAND (unit should complete assignment unless it is an emergency).
CALL DISPATCHER BY TELEPHONE (dispatcher should give the phone number if unknown).
STAND BY (used when advising units to wait for a message).

questions.stem: Match each code with the special usage instruction from Procedure 104.
answer: Should NOT be used if a transmission was not heard or understood.
To be used when a message was not heard or understood.
Only used when the dispatcher wants to know the unit’s current location.
